operations.name: Saw Cut Blank
operations.setup_note: Saw a discrete blank from round stock, leaving allowance for facing. The assumed starting blank is solid round stock.

operations.name: CNC Lathe – Bore and Rough Turn
operations.setup_note: Chuck the saw-cut blank on its outside diameter and face the open end to establish an axial reference. Rough the accessible outside lands, then bore from the open end while retaining the closed bottom wall.

operations.name: CNC Lathe – Finish Turn
operations.setup_note: Grip on the finished bore with an expanding mandrel so the thin wall is supported while the outside diameters are finished. Face the opposite end to length and finish the OD details.

operations.name: VMC – Axial Hole Pattern
operations.setup_note: Locate the finished part from the turned surfaces and orient the closed end wall for axial drilling. Pick up drawing datum A for the four-hole bolt-circle position; its physical datum mapping needs confirmation.

operations.name: Deburr
operations.setup_note: Remove sharp edges and drilling burrs, observing the drawing note to break all sharp edges 0.5 mm maximum.

operations.name: Final Inspection
operations.setup_note: Inspect the turned diameters, bore, overall length, hole sizes, bolt-circle position, and edge condition against the drawing.

clarifications.question: Is the supplied blank a solid round blank, or is it a formed cup/tube blank?
clarifications.suggested_default: Proceed from solid round stock and form the cavity by blind boring.

clarifications.question: Are F06 (Ø128) and F09 (Ø126.21) separate axial OD lands, and where does each land extend?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat them as distinct OD lands, with F06 the larger diameter and F09 the smaller diameter.

clarifications.question: Which physical face or feature is drawing datum A for the four-hole position tolerance?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the designated end face and turned axis as the VMC setup references, subject to confirmation against the drawing.

clarifications.question: Do the four F05 bolt-circle holes pass through the bottom wall?
clarifications.suggested_default: Assume all four holes pass through the bottom wall.

assumptions.text: Because the blank type is unstated and the available stock forms do not include a formed cup, assume a solid round blank and use hot_rolled_round_bar as the closest available form. This stock choice should be confirmed because ASTM A622M is not identified as hot-rolled bar.
Treat F06 and F09 as distinct OD lands; exact axial extents are not present in the routing view.
Assume F04 and F05 are holes through the closed bottom wall; the depth of the F05 pattern is not specified.
Omit center drilling for lathe support because the part's length-to-diameter ratio is below 4:1 and the planned setups use chuck and expanding-mandrel holding.
Omit lathe grooving and threading because no groove or thread features are identified. Omit part-off because the route starts with discrete saw-cut blanks rather than bar-fed production.
Drill the 13.25 mm holes directly after spotting: the specified size range does not call for reaming, no hole exceeds the pilot-drilling threshold, and no deep-hole condition is identified.
